claim.why_it_matters: The stage table is broken: its header row is a stray paragraph, so 'COPY statement | Text manipulation' became the table's header row; the second header 'Compiler directives | Stage' is an ordinary data row; and the FLAG-NATIVE-ARITHMETIC row is ejected from the table into a paragraph, splitting it into two tables.

verdict.reasoning: Checked against the printed page (PDF p60, printed page 36, §2014:7.1). The printed page has two plain two-column lists, each under an underlined header: 'Compiler directing statements / Stage' (COPY statement, an indented SUPPRESS phrase, REPLACE statement) and 'Compiler directives / Stage' (CALL-CONVENTION through TURN). The markdown keeps every entry and pairs each name with the stage the PDF gives it. That includes FLAG-NATIVE-ARITHMETIC Compilation, which sits in the right order between FLAG-85 and IF and is only set as a paragraph. The claim describes the markdown accurately, but the problem it describes is table markup: a header line set as a paragraph, a data row promoted to a table header, and one row pulled out as a paragraph. These are formatting artifacts of the layout. No text is missing or changed, and every name-to-stage pairing still reads correctly, so a reader comes away with the same meaning. Under the rejection criteria (formatting only, meaning unchanged), this is not a genuine content discrepancy.
